researched_by: Somerset Council's own car parks and pay-and-display guidance (which is still partitioned by former district and was read in all four district variants), its individual car park location pages, its coaches/motorcycles/motorhomes page, its traffic regulation order register, its PSPO register and ONS postcode centroids
policy_summary:
SOMERSET PERMITS OVERNIGHT PARKING IN ITS CAR PARKS, IN WRITING, ACROSS THE WHOLE COUNTY. Under the heading 'Overnight parking' the council's own guidance says: 'You can park overnight but you will need to check the terms of the car park you intend to park and ensure, if required, that you have paid for a parking session which will cover the start of enforcement the following day.' That sentence appears identically in all four former-district versions of the page, so it is the settled county-wide position and not a leftover from one predecessor. It is close to the most permissive published position in the dataset. Nearly every other English authority researched so far either prohibits overnight parking outright or is silent; Somerset affirmatively allows it and then tells you how to do it properly.

The only vehicle exclusion is narrow: 'Please note, caravans and lorries over 7.5 tonnes may not use car parks provided by the Council.' A caravan is out. A motorhome is not mentioned and is therefore in. Most Somerset car parks carry a 'No height restrictions' label and '24 hour access', and the standard charging window is 9am to 6pm, so a van that parks at 7pm pays nothing until 9am the next morning, at which point a ticket is needed. That is the whole regime.

AND SOMERSET SAYS NOTHING WHATEVER ABOUT SLEEPING. There is no clause about sleeping, camping, living in a vehicle, cooking or awnings anywhere in the published guidance - not on the car park pages, not on the motorhome page, not in any permit condition found. Compare Torbay forty miles south, which sells an overnight ticket and simultaneously bans 'Overnight sleeping in vehicles or camping'. Somerset has the permission without the carve-out. On the published material a motorhome parked overnight in a Somerset car park, paid up for the morning, is doing nothing the council has prohibited.

On-street is permissive too, and unusually explicit: 'You can park a motorhome or any vehicle on a residential street without restrictions, as long as it doesn't block anything and has a valid MOT and road tax. However, in areas where you need a resident permit, there are size limits on vehicles.' No motor-caravan waiting restriction, no seafront no-overnight-parking order and no camping PSPO was found anywhere in Somerset.

There is NO PROVISION in the designated sense. No aire, no motorhome bays, no overnight permit product, no waste disposal point, no self-containment scheme, no charge for staying rather than parking. Somerset has not built anything; it has simply declined to forbid. Two of the 141 council car parks carry a 'Motorhomes/caravans' facility label - Butt Close in Glastonbury and Cattle Market in Frome - and Butt Close's page says 'Motorhomes, caravans and trailers can park here - payment must be made for the number of spaces used', which flatly contradicts the county-wide 'caravans ... may not use car parks provided by the Council'. Both statements are live on the same website.

LEGACY DISTRICT ORDERS STILL APPLY, AND THE COUNCIL SAYS SO. Somerset Council was created in April 2023 from Somerset County Council plus Mendip, Sedgemoor, South Somerset and Somerset West and Taunton. Three years on, the parking pages still open with a district chooser and the explanation 'We are now a single council but at the moment some services are different depending on where they are', offering Mendip (East), Sedgemoor (North), Somerset West and Taunton (West) and South Somerset (South). The differences are real and not cosmetic: Blue Badge terms diverge on the face of the guidance - 'an allowance of an additional 1 hour time is granted free of charge in all pay and display car parks only. In the Mendip and Sedgemoor area parking is free when a valid Blue Badge is displayed.' A single consolidated Somerset off-street parking places order would not produce two different Blue Badge concessions. The traffic order register tells the same story: a live proposal dated 29 July 2026 is titled 'Mendip Amendment No.36', still amending the predecessor district's order by its old name. The PSPO register is likewise filed under Somerset East (Mendip), Somerset North (Sedgemoor), Somerset West and Taunton and Somerset South. The honest answer to the question is therefore YES - the four legacy district off-street parking orders remain the operative instruments, harmonised in presentation but not in law.

Coastally this matters most at Blue Anchor, between Minehead and Watchet, which is a free, unbarriered, 156-space, no-height-restriction, 24-hour council car park a few metres from the beach, in a county that says you can park overnight. Watchet has Anchor Street and Burnham-on-Sea has the Berrow Road (Discount) car park, both long stay, both 24-hour, both without height limits.
notes:
The single most useful line in this file is the permission, and the reason it is worth trusting is that it survives the district test. Somerset's website is still four websites in a trenchcoat, and almost every parking fact on it changes when you switch district. The overnight sentence and the caravan exclusion do not. They are identical under Mendip, Sedgemoor and South Somerset, which is the strongest available evidence that this is genuine county policy rather than an inherited Sedgemoor paragraph nobody has revisited.

The parking-versus-sleeping distinction is doing all the work here and a user should understand its limits. Somerset has authorised the PARKING. It has not authorised the SLEEPING, because it has not addressed sleeping at all. Silence is not permission in the way that 'You can park overnight' is permission, and an officer who wanted to act would reach for the legacy district order's conditions of use, which are not published on the website and which this research could not read. The realistic position is that a motorhome parked and paid for is lawful, and that what happens inside it has no published rule against it - but the underlying order text is the gap in this file, not a settled answer.

The caravan contradiction is not trivial and should be reported to the council rather than resolved by guesswork. 'Caravans ... may not use car parks provided by the Council' is a county-wide prohibition; 'Motorhomes, caravans and trailers can park here' is a specific permission on a specific car park page, with the payment mechanism spelled out. A user towing a caravan into Butt Close on the strength of the second sentence and receiving a PCN under the first would have a strong informal case and no clear formal one.

Direction of travel: harmonisation of charges, silence on motorhomes. Somerset has spent the post-vesting period aligning tariffs and machines - a common PayByPhone estate, a common MiPermit season ticket portal, a common 9am-6pm charging window across most sites - while leaving the underlying orders and the Blue Badge concessions unaligned. Nothing found suggests motorhome or overnight use has ever been considered as an issue in either direction: no consultation, no report, no signage scheme, no news release. Somerset is permissive by inheritance and inattention rather than by decision, which is a materially less stable form of permission than South Ayrshire's, where the bays were built on purpose.

EXMOOR HOUSE, DULVERTON IS RESOLVED, AND IT RESOLVES AGAINST THE NATIONAL PARK. The Exmoor file flagged that Exmoor National Park Authority lists Exmoor House as its own pay-and-display 'weekends only' while Somerset publishes a car park of the same name. Somerset's location page settles the operational question: Exmoor House car park, Dulverton, TA22 9HL, 42 standard plus 3 disabled plus 2 EV bays, charging 9am to 6pm daily including public and bank holidays, 24-hour access, no height restriction, run by Somerset Council, with Somerset's tariff (GBP1.00 for an hour to GBP5.80 all day) and Somerset's season tickets. There is no second car park and no weekday/weekend split in Somerset's description. Exmoor House is the National Park Authority's headquarters building, which is almost certainly why ENPA lists the car park at all, but the parking place itself is Somerset's and is operated under Somerset's regime seven days a week. The consequence for a van user is a genuine reversal: under ENPA's 'no overnight parking or camping' condition of entry the answer at Exmoor House would be no, and under Somerset's 'You can park overnight' the answer is yes. The exmoor-national-park.json record for Exmoor House should be reassigned to Somerset or downgraded; it is currently the only ENPA restriction record in that file resting on a car park ENPA does not appear to run.

The wider Exmoor boundary point stands and is worth restating from the Somerset side. Inside the National Park, Somerset owns the town car parks - Dulverton, Dunster, Porlock, Exford's village parking, Minehead - while ENPA owns the moorland ones and the National Trust owns County Gate, Webbers Post, Horner and Bossington. Three landowners, three regimes, no signposting between them, and they now point in opposite directions on the only question a van user cares about. A driver refused at an ENPA moorland car park can legitimately drive down into Dulverton or Porlock and park overnight in a Somerset one.

STEP-2 SWEEP, 27 July 2026 - country parks, council caravan and holiday parks including leased ones, harbours and marinas, and sites inherited from the four districts in 2023 were all checked. Somerset Council runs NO campsite, caravan park, touring site or holiday park, directly or on lease. Its countryside estate does not live on somerset.gov.uk at all - the /locations/ URLs redirect to a separate microsite, discover-wild-somerset.co.uk, run by the council's Green Estates team - and it lists five sites: Ham Hill Country Park, Chard Reservoir LNR, Berrow Dunes LNR, Wilstock and Stockmoor Country Park, and Moldrams LNR. None has camping. Ham Hill, the obvious candidate at 160ha with a ranger team and visitor centre, actively bans it: park4night reports signs put up banning overnight sleeping with ranger patrols to enforce, and the working quarries inside the park are Duchy of Cornwall land, not council. Apex Park, Burnham-on-Sea (ex-Sedgemoor) is free to park but 'overnight stops by campers are not allowed'. Yeovil Country Park has left council ownership entirely under the Yeovil devolution programme and is now Yeovil Town Council's.

The one asset that fits the shape of the question and still fails it: Somerset Council is the statutory harbour authority for WATCHET and MINEHEAD, and owns the freehold of Watchet Marina, which was leased to Watchet Harbour Marina Ltd in 2001 and is now managed by Western Marinas Limited, which took the marina assets over from The Marine and Property Group Ltd. It is a boat marina. The harbour regulations cover moorings, boat specifications, chains and harbour dues and say nothing about vehicles, camping, motorhomes or caravans. No vehicle overnight product exists at Watchet, Minehead, Burnham or Dunball. Worth knowing separately: Harbour Road car park in Watchet (TA23 0AQ) is a Somerset Council long-stay with no height restriction, 24-hour access and two dedicated motorhome bays at ordinary daily and weekly tariffs - but no overnight policy, permit or facilities, and park4night users reported 'no overnight camping' signs in May-June 2026.

Also checked and not provision: SSE Outdoors, the council's residential outdoor education service (Kilve Court, The Outdoor Centre at Kilve, Great Wood, Charterhouse) - all bunkhouses and heated cabins on exclusive group booking, no tent, caravan or motorhome pitches. What Sedgemoor DC actually held on the Brean coast was beach management, not caravan sites; Somerset Council today manages Burnham-on-Sea, Brean and Berrow beaches, parking only. Private supply, do not re-research as council: Holiday Resort Unity, Northam Farm, Warren Farm and Brean Leisure at Brean; Butlin's Minehead; Haven Burnham-on-Sea and Haven Doniford Bay; Blue Anchor Bay parks; Dunster Beach chalets; and the CAMC certificated locations around Burnham and Ham Hill.
open_questions: WHAT DO THE LEGACY DISTRICT OFF-STREET PARKING ORDERS ACTUALLY SAY? None of the four (Mendip, Sedgemoor, South Somerset, Somerset West and Taunton) could be located as a document on somerset.gov.uk. The TRO register carries 745 items but is not searchable by title through a plain URL and returned no order with 'Off Street' or 'Parking Places' in its name on the readable page. Somebody should request all four orders and check their conditions-of-use clauses for sleeping, camping and cooking - that is the one thing that could overturn the reading in this file.

Is there a single consolidated Somerset Council off-street parking places order in preparation? The Blue Badge divergence and the 'Mendip Amendment No.36' naming say no as at July 2026, but a consolidation would be the obvious next step and would be the moment the overnight permission could quietly change.

Does any car park carry site-specific signage prohibiting overnight stays or sleeping, notwithstanding the county-wide permission? Signage was not inspected anywhere. The guidance's own instruction to 'check the terms of the car park you intend to park' implies terms exist per site.
The caravan contradiction: are caravans permitted at Butt Close, Glastonbury and Cattle Market, Frome as their pages say, or excluded as the county-wide rule says? Only the council can answer this.

The car park directory is paginated client-side and only the first alphabetical page (Abbey Street to Churchfields) could be read. The 'Motorhomes/caravans' facility label may appear on further car parks between D and Y that this research could not see. The full count of motorhome-labelled sites is unknown - two confirmed out of 141.

Somerset TraffWeb (somerset.traffweb.app) is the definitive on-street restriction map and is a JavaScript application that could not be read. Any motor-caravan or overnight waiting restriction on the Burnham-on-Sea, Minehead or Watchet seafronts would show there and nowhere else.

Is Blue Anchar car park genuinely unrestricted overnight? It is free, unbarriered, 24-hour, 156 spaces and on the coast, which is exactly the profile that attracts a restriction once it becomes popular. No restriction is published now. Worth re-checking each season.

What is the enforcement reality? NSL Ltd enforces on Somerset's behalf. Nothing found indicates whether patrols run at night at all, which matters more here than elsewhere because the published rule is permissive and the risk is a site-specific exception rather than a general ban.

Minehead's seafront car parks (Warren Road, Seaward Way, The Parade area) could not be reached by URL guess and were not on the readable page of the directory. Minehead is the largest coastal town in the county and its car park terms are unverified.

A ground lease of council land to a Brean or Berrow caravan operator cannot be ruled out from public pages alone - it would only show in committee papers or an FOI'd asset register. democracy.somerset.gov.uk was not trawled. The council's disposal messaging describes its saleable estate only as 'non-operational buildings and small parcels of land' and says asset detail 'remains commercially confidential'.

Harbour Road car park, Watchet: the council's own page says Somerset Council operates it, park4night attributes it to Watchet Town Council, and users report recent no-overnight-camping signage. Whose car park is it and what changed?

sites.name: All Somerset Council car parks (overnight parking permitted, no designated bays)
sites.notes: THE COUNTY-WIDE PERMISSION, AND THE WHOLE OF IT. Verbatim, under the heading 'Overnight parking': 'You can park overnight but you will need to check the terms of the car park you intend to park and ensure, if required, that you have paid for a parking session which will cover the start of enforcement the following day.' Verified identical under the Mendip, Sedgemoor and South Somerset versions of the page. The standard charging window across the estate is 9am to 6pm daily including bank holidays, so the overnight hours themselves are unpriced - price_per_night is recorded as 0 for that reason, not because the stay is free of obligation: you must hold a valid session covering 9am the following morning or you will be issued a PCN. time_from and time_to record the unpriced window, not an opening or closing time; most Somerset car parks are labelled '24 hour access' with 'No height restrictions'. This is a PERMISSION TO PARK ONLY. Somerset designates no motorhome bays, sells no overnight permit, provides no waste disposal or chemical point anywhere in the county, and imposes no self-containment requirement. It also says nothing at all about sleeping, camping or cooking - there is no such clause anywhere in the published guidance. Instrument recorded as policy_only because the underlying legal instruments are the four unconsolidated legacy district off-street parking orders, none of which could be located as documents.

sites.name: All Somerset Council car parks - caravans and lorries over 7.5 tonnes excluded
sites.notes: The only published vehicle exclusion, verbatim from the 'Off street parking' section: 'Please note, caravans and lorries over 7.5 tonnes may not use car parks provided by the Council.' applies_to is recorded as 'unknown' because the schema has no value for a towed-caravan-and-HGV exclusion: this is a vehicle-TYPE ban, not a ban on vehicles adapted for sleeping, not a DVLA motor caravan ban and not a length limit. THE IMPORTANT WORD IS THE ONE THAT IS ABSENT. Motorhomes, campervans and motor caravans are not named and are therefore not excluded; several Somerset car parks positively advertise motorhome parking. Confidence is medium rather than high only because the rule is directly contradicted on the council's own site: Butt Close car park in Glastonbury states 'Motorhomes, caravans and trailers can park here' and both Butt Close and Cattle Market in Frome carry a 'Motorhomes/caravans' facility label in the directory. Both statements are currently published.

sites.name: Blue Anchor Car Park, Minehead (free, overnight parking permitted)
sites.search_hint: Blue Anchor car park, Minehead, Somerset
sites.notes: THE BEST SINGLE FIND IN SOMERSET. A free long-stay council car park on the coast at Blue Anchor, between Minehead and Watchet, with 156 standard bays and 4 disabled bays, 'no height restrictions' and '24 hour access', in a county whose published rule is that you can park overnight. No charge at any hour, so nothing to buy for the following morning either - the one practical obligation attached to the county-wide permission does not bite here. No barrier, no machine, no attendant, no waste facilities and no designated motorhome bay: this is ordinary free parking that happens to be legal overnight, not an aire. Blue Anchor sits just outside the Exmoor National Park boundary, which matters because ENPA car parks a few miles inland prohibit exactly what is permitted here. Caravans are excluded by the county-wide rule. Verify signage on arrival - a free unbarriered seafront car park is the single most likely candidate in the county for a site-specific restriction being added.
sites.geocode_precision: ONS centroid of TA24 6LD, the postcode Somerset Council publishes for Blue Anchor car park, on the coast at Blue Anchor

sites.name: Butt Close Car Park, Glastonbury (motorhome parking advertised)
sites.notes: One of only two Somerset car parks carrying a 'Motorhomes/caravans' facility label in the council directory, and the one whose page states the position outright: 'Motorhomes, caravans and trailers can park here - payment must be made for the number of spaces used.' Long stay, 'no height restrictions and 24 hour access', 74 standard bays plus 3 disabled and 6 EV. Charging 9am to 6pm daily including bank holidays, GBP1.30 an hour to GBP6.80 all day, so the overnight hours are free but a session covering 9am the next morning is required. Combined with the county-wide 'You can park overnight', this is about as close as Somerset comes to sanctioned motorhome overnight parking - in the middle of Glastonbury, ten miles inland. THE CARAVAN SENTENCE HERE CONTRADICTS THE COUNTY-WIDE RULE that 'caravans and lorries over 7.5 tonnes may not use car parks provided by the Council'. No waste disposal, no chemical point, no designated motorhome bay - you buy as many ordinary bays as you cover.
sites.geocode_precision: ONS centroid of BA6 9HY, the postcode Somerset Council publishes for Butt Close car park

sites.name: Cattle Market Car Park, Frome (motorhome parking advertised)
sites.search_hint: Cattle Market car park, Bridge Street, Frome
sites.notes: The largest car park in the county estate and the other one labelled 'Motorhomes/caravans': 352 standard bays plus 23 disabled, 6 EV and 1 motorcycle, public toilets on site, 'no height restrictions' and '24 hour access'. Charging 9am to 6pm daily, GBP1.30 an hour to GBP6.80 all day, GBP2.30 all day Sunday. Motorhomes and caravans pay for the number of spaces used. THE DETAIL WORTH NOTING IS THE HGV TARIFF: Cattle Market has an explicit overnight product for lorries - HGVs may park 6pm to 9am at GBP11.60 - which is the only priced overnight stay found anywhere in Somerset. It proves the council is perfectly capable of writing an overnight tariff when it wants one; it has simply never written one for motorhomes, which instead fall under the free-after-6pm rule with the rest of the estate. Toilets on site make this the best-equipped realistic overnight stop in Somerset, though it is a working town-centre car park in Frome with no waste disposal for vans.
sites.geocode_precision: ONS centroid of BA11 1BE, the postcode Somerset Council publishes for Cattle Market car park, Bridge Street

sites.name: Anchor Street Car Park, Watchet (overnight parking permitted)
sites.notes: Watchet's town-centre long-stay car park, a short walk from the harbour and the marina. 26 standard bays plus 3 disabled - small, and it will fill. 'No height restrictions and 24 hour access'. Charging 9am to 6pm daily including bank holidays; GBP1.30 an hour, GBP6.40 all day, GBP30 a week. Card as well as coins at the machine, which is not true of every Somerset site. Covered by the county-wide overnight permission and by the county-wide caravan exclusion. No motorhome bay and no facilities of any kind for vans.
sites.geocode_precision: ONS centroid of TA23 0AZ, the postcode Somerset Council publishes for Anchor Street car park, Watchet

sites.name: Discount (Berrow Road) Car Park, Burnham-on-Sea (overnight parking permitted)
sites.search_hint: Discount car park, Berrow Road, Burnham-on-Sea
sites.notes: Burnham-on-Sea's main long-stay car park, on Berrow Road a few minutes from the seafront, and the cheapest of the coastal three: GBP0.90 an hour, GBP4.60 all day, charging 9am to 6pm daily. 112 standard bays plus 3 disabled, 'no height restrictions', '24 hour access'. THE CAVEAT THAT PUTS THIS AT MEDIUM CONFIDENCE is a published maximum stay of 1 day. Read strictly, that is a limit on the length of a single stay rather than on being there overnight, and it sits alongside the county-wide permission without either page acknowledging the other; read unhelpfully, it is the kind of term the overnight guidance means when it tells you to 'check the terms of the car park you intend to park'. One night is safe on any reading; a second consecutive night is not. max_nights is recorded as 1 on that basis.
sites.geocode_precision: ONS centroid of TA8 2ET, the postcode Somerset Council publishes for the Discount (Berrow Road) car park, Burnham-on-Sea

sites.name: Exmoor House Car Park, Dulverton (Somerset Council, inside Exmoor National Park)
sites.notes: THE EXMOOR AMBIGUITY, RESOLVED IN SOMERSET'S FAVOUR. exmoor-national-park.json flagged that Exmoor National Park Authority lists Exmoor House as its own pay-and-display 'weekends only' while Somerset publishes a car park of the same name at the same place. Somerset's location page describes one car park, run by Somerset Council, charging 9am to 6pm DAILY including public and bank holidays, with 42 standard bays plus 3 disabled and 2 EV, 24-hour access, no height restriction, Somerset's tariff (GBP1.00 an hour to GBP5.80 all day) and Somerset's season tickets. It makes no reference to the National Park Authority, to weekends, or to a second car park. Exmoor House is ENPA's headquarters building, which explains why the Authority lists the car park at all, but the parking place is operated as Somerset's seven days a week. THE PRACTICAL CONSEQUENCE IS A REVERSAL: ENPA's estate-wide condition of entry is 'no overnight parking or camping', so under ENPA's rules the answer here is no; Somerset's rule is 'You can park overnight', so under Somerset's rules the answer is yes. Confidence is medium because ENPA has not withdrawn its own listing and no signage was inspected - if a sign in this car park carries ENPA's terms, ENPA's terms are what a warden will quote. This is the one place in the dataset where two authorities publish opposite answers about the same tarmac.
sites.geocode_precision: ONS centroid of TA22 9HL, the postcode both Somerset Council and Exmoor National Park Authority publish for Exmoor House, Dulverton

sites.name: On-street parking throughout Somerset (motorhomes permitted on residential streets)
sites.notes: Somerset publishes an unusually explicit on-street position on its motorhome page: 'You can park a motorhome or any vehicle on a residential street without restrictions, as long as it doesn't block anything and has a valid MOT and road tax. However, in areas where you need a resident permit, there are size limits on vehicles.' That is a statement of the general law rather than a Somerset concession, but few authorities say it out loud and fewer still say it on a page about motorhomes. NO MOTOR-CARAVAN WAITING RESTRICTION WAS FOUND ANYWHERE IN SOMERSET - no seafront no-overnight-parking order at Burnham-on-Sea, Minehead or Watchet, no height or length bar on any named road, and no camping PSPO (the county's PSPOs, still filed under Somerset East/North/West/South, cover dogs, street drinking and begging only). Confidence is medium because the definitive source is Somerset TraffWeb, a JavaScript restriction map that could not be read; a localised order could exist there without appearing in the guidance. Ordinary waiting restrictions, resident permit zones and obstruction of course still apply.
